questions.q: Can AI replace a business strategy?
questions.a: No. AI can't give you direction, fix a weak business model or create customers you don't already have. What it does well is speed up a strategy you've already set. If your direction is wrong, AI simply gets you to the wrong place faster.

questions.q: How should AI fit into my business strategy?
questions.a: Start with your strategy, then use AI to amplify what's already working. A restaurant that knows its guest journey, for example, can use AI to shorten service time, drive repeat visits and recover unhappy guests quickly. The question to ask is where AI helps you deliver on a plan you already have.

questions.q: What is vertical AI, and why is it growing?
questions.a: Vertical AI is built for a specific industry or workflow, such as scheduling, routing, hiring or responding to customers. It's growing because it understands the context of that work, including your language and your data. That context keeps your strategy in control of how the tool behaves.

questions.q: Where does AI support strategy best?
questions.a: AI is most useful where it frees people for judgment calls. In operations it cuts noise so your team can focus on exceptions, and in marketing it speeds up content and campaign cycles. In finance it spots anomalies early, and in customer experience it resolves routine issues quickly while flagging what needs a person.

questions.q: What happens when a company adopts AI without a strategy?
questions.a: You usually end up with dashboards nobody checks, automation nobody trusts and systems that solve problems nobody had. That makes AI expensive noise. Clear goals for why you're automating each task are what turn it into an advantage competitors can't copy quickly.
